sources.entry: Cate - IDE built on an infinite zoomable canvas. Editor, terminal, browser, and AI agent panels float in a spatial workspace instead of tabs.

Cate by 0-AI UG - A cross-platform desktop IDE built on an infinite zoomable canvas, where editors, terminals, browsers, and docs float in freeform space instead of tabs — and ships skills that let Claude Code spawn agent terminals on the canvas, coordinate through canvas notes, and drive browser panels. A genuinely novel UX, well-engineered (CI, e2e tests, context-isolated IPC, scoped filesystem

summary.one_liner: Cate is an infinite-canvas IDE for running parallel coding agents, where terminals, editors, browsers and other panels float on a zoomable workspace instead of in tabs.
summary.what_it_does: Cate runs Claude Code, Codex, or any agent CLI inside its terminal panels and shows whether each agent is working, finished, or waiting for input, with notifications when one needs an answer. It can create a git worktree and branch (from a local branch, remote branch, or open PR) with its own colored area on the canvas. Panels include terminals, Monaco editors, browsers, PDF/image/DOCX viewers, and nested canvases, which can float, dock into tabs and splits, or detach into separate windows. It also provides multi-repo git source control, git badges in the file tree, side-by-side diffs, ripgrep search, and a Cmd+K command palette. A bundled "cate" CLI lets agents drive browser panels, read other terminals, open files, and manage panels. Workspaces can run locally or on another machine, and another device can join a live workspace via QR or pairing code.
use_cases: run multiple coding agents in parallel
manage git worktrees for separate branches
how_to_run: Download a prebuilt release from the project's releases page (macOS DMG/ZIP, Windows NSIS/ZIP, Linux AppImage/DEB/tar.gz)
notable: Agent-aware terminals that report running, waiting, or finished state and notify on permission prompts
Git worktree creation per branch with its own colored canvas territory
Agent sessions reattach with resume commands after restart
Local and remote workspaces with end-to-end encrypted device pairing via QR code or Cate Connect
No config files: opening a folder creates a workspace
caveats: Build-from-source is discouraged for daily use; the README points to prebuilt releases and a CONTRIBUTING.md for building
Cate Connect pairing is referenced but its details are not described in the README
keywords: work on several branches at once
